subject: Renewal & capacity sync — Q4 co-term + surge protection
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Leah Morris <leah.morris@brightframe.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & capacity sync — Q4 co-term + surge protection

Leah —

Quick note as we start the renewal window for BrightFrame: your Q4 usage trend shows the usual seasonal uptick and the customer success team flagged a potential burst next November. We want to propose a renewal structure that: 1) aligns your term to calendar-year co-term (co-terming both clusters to 12/31 start), 2) stages the committed capacity across the first 6 months (light ramp -> full commitment), and 3) introduces a short "surge safeguard" pool that BrightFrame can consume during the first 90 days of a heavy spike without immediate overage charges.

High-level ask from our side: can you share any procurement windows or blackout dates (quiet windows) in Q4 that we should avoid for billing or contract switchovers? If you want, I can draft a short SOW and a simple schedule that shows the staged commits and the surge pool cap.

If it helps, I can loop in Camila (AM) and Marissa (my manager) to walk through ramp timing and possible uptake credits for early consumption.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0118

[Attachment: usage_snapshot_Q2_summary.pdf]

From: Leah Morris <leah.morris@brightframe.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@brightframe.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity sync — Q4 co-term + surge protection

Karthik —

Thanks for the heads-up. A few quick notes from our side: 1) Procurement prefers any contract changes to occur outside our fiscal close week (first week of December) — that's our quiet window; 2) we have an internal constraint that auto-renew clauses need explicit opt-out windows and a one-cycle notice for price changes; and 3) on SLAs we need to confirm whether Dedicated capacity commitments have a higher uptime SLA vs hosted API.

Before committing, procurement will want the SOW, a clear start/end of billing period, and a sample invoice cadence. Please include an explicit toggled option for auto-renew (on/off) and an explanation of the surge safeguard billing: is it prepaid, reserve, or invoiced after consumption?

Looping in procurement on cc.

Best,
Leah Morris
Head of Cloud Ops | BrightFrame
leah.morris@brightframe.com

[ProcureOps: please confirm the quiet window dates and any contraints on co-terming across business units.]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Leah Morris <leah.morris@brightframe.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity sync — Q4 co-term + surge protection

Thanks Leah — 

Appreciate the clarity on the quiet window (first week of December) and the auto-renew requirement. I've drafted a short SOW and a staged-commit schedule for your review; attaching a first draft. The surge safeguard is modeled two ways in the draft: (A) a 90-day reserve bucket (prepaid credit that draws down) or (B) a short-term invoiceable surge with a capped monthly max and a waived overage for the first two surges in the 90-day window. Camila — can you confirm which of these aligns better with BrightFrame's operational preference? Marissa — from a commercial perspective we carved a modest early-uptake credit if BrightFrame hits 60% of the first stage in month one.

Action items:
- Leah: confirm preference for reserve vs invoiceable surge (reply to all)
- Procurement: confirm quiet window date formally (ProcureOps)
- Camila: I'll let you run the ops feasibility check and indicate any technical caveats for dedicated vs hosted SLA.

Attaching: BrightFrame_SOW_v2.pdf (draft), usage_snapshot_Q2_summary.pdf

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

[Attachment: BrightFrame_SOW_v2.pdf]

From: ProcureOps <procureops@brightframe.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity sync — Q4 co-term + surge protection

Team —

Procurement reviewed the draft SOW and we have a few redlines before we can route for approval: 
- Add explicit auto-renew opt-out step with a 60-day notice window (we cannot accept open automatic renew without opt-out flow).
- Invoice cadence must be quarterly-in-advance or monthly arrears; please provide both options with the impact to pricing.
- SLA: we require 99.9% uptime for mission-critical dedicated clusters and a defined credit table for downtime beyond thresholds.
- For the surge safeguard, procurement prefers a prepaid reserve model (option A) but wants a clear refund/rollover policy if unused after 90 days.

Please provide a revised SOW with those items called out and a sample invoice showing the staged ramp (month 1: 20% commit, month 2: 40%, month 3-6: 40% -> full). Also include a short legal clause on termination for convenience (90-day notice) and an explicit start-of-term definition (billing start vs technically available date).

Thanks —
ProcureOps Team
procureops@brightframe.com

[Attached: procurement_redlines_0701.pdf]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Leah Morris <leah.morris@brightframe.com>, ProcureOps <procureops@brightframe.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity sync — Q4 co-term + surge protection

Leah / ProcureOps —

Thanks for the redlines. We've updated the SOW and the commercial appendix to reflect: 1) explicit auto-renew opt-out flow (60-day notice), 2) both invoice cadence options with the associated small discount for quarterly-in-advance, 3) a 99.9% dedicated-cluster uptime SLA with a graduated credit table, and 4) the surge safeguard as a prepaid reserve with a 30% rollover credit if unused after 90 days (applied to next invoice within the same fiscal year). We've also clarified the start-of-term: billing begins the first day of the next calendar month after signature; technical availability can be scheduled up to 72 hours prior at no additional charge.

I've attached BrightFrame_SOW_v3.pdf (clean) and a Q2 usage report for your finance team to verify charge estimates. If these updates are acceptable, I'll prep the DocuSign packet and include both invoice cadence options so procurement can route internally.

Next steps from our side:
- Finalize DocuSign envelope (Jordan)
- Camila to confirm operations readiness window for a planned November surge test (if you want us to reserve the surge pool for that period)
- Karthik/Marissa to prepare the commercial approval memo.

Jordan Blake
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

[Attachments: BrightFrame_SOW_v3.pdf, BrightFrame_usage_report_Q2.csv]
